and she gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no space in the guest room.
There were shepherds living in the fields nearby and keeping watch over their flocks at night.
Suddenly, an angel of the Lord stood among them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.
The angel said to them, “Y’all don’t be afraid! I am bringing y’all good news that will bring great joy to all the people.
For today in the city of David, a Savior has been born to y’all. He is Christ the Lord.
This will be a sign to y’all: y’all will find a baby wrapped in cloth and lying in a feeding trough.”
Suddenly, a vast heavenly army appeared with the angel praising God and saying,
“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, peace toward the humans ʜᴇ is pleased with.”
When the angels left them and went back to heaven, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened and that the Lord has made known to us.”
So they hurried off and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the feeding trough.
After they saw him, they spread the word that had been spoken to them about this child,
and all who heard it marveled at the things the shepherds said to them.
But Mary treasured all these things, pondering them in her heart.
The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things they had heard and seen, just as they had been told.

verses.heading: The Circumcision and Presentation of Jesus / The Circumcision and Presentation of Jesus
verses.text: When eight days had passed and it was time to circumcise the child, he was named Jesus, the name the angel had given him before he was conceived in the womb.
When the time came for their purification according to the Law of Moses, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord
(as it is written in the Law of the Lord, “Every male who opens the womb is to be dedicated to the Lord [YHWH]”),
and to offer a sacrifice according to what is said in the Law of the Lord, “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”

verses.heading: Two Saints Recognize Jesus as Christ / Two Saints Recognize Jesus as Christ
verses.text: Now, there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon, who was righteous and devout. He was looking for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was on him.
It had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not die before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
Guided by the Spirit, he went into the temple. When the parents brought in the child Jesus to perform for him what was customary in the Law,
Simeon took him into his arms and blessed God, saying,
“Now Sovereign Master, you can dismiss your slave in peace, according to your promise.
For my eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared in the presence of all people groups,
a light for revelation to the ethnic groups, and the glory of your people Israel.”
The child’s father and mother marveled at the things that were being said about him.
Simeon blessed them, and said to Mary, his mother, “Indeed, this child is destined to cause the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be spoken against.
—and a sword will pierce through your own soul—that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
There was also a prophetess, Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was quite old, having lived with her husband seven years after her virginity,
and then was a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never departed from the temple, serving night and day through fasting and prayer.
At that moment, she came up to them and began to give thanks to God and to speak of the child to everyone who was expectantly awaiting the redemption of Jerusalem.
When they had done everything according to the Law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own city, Nazareth.
The child continued to grow and become strong, increasing in wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.

verses.heading: Young Jesus Visits the Temple / Young Jesus Visits the Temple
verses.text: Every year, Jesus’s parents went to Jerusalem for the Feast of the Passover.
When he was twelve years old, they went there again according to the custom of the Feast.
When they feast was over, as they were returning home, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, but his parents didn’t know it.
Thinking he was in their company, they went on a day’s journey. Then they began looking for him among their relatives and friends.
When they didn’t find him, they returned to Jerusalem to look for him.
After three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
Everyone who heard him was amazed at his understanding and his answers.
When his parents saw him, they were astonished. His mother said to him, “Son, why have you treated us like this? See, your father and I have been anxiously looking for you.”
“Why were y’all looking for me?” he replied. “Didn’t y’all know I had to be in my Father’s house?”
verses.html: “Why were y’all looking for me?” he replied. “Didn’t y’all know I had to be in my Father’s house?”

verses.text: But they didn’t understand what he was saying to them.
Then he went down with them to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. But his mother kept all these things in her heart.
And Jesus continued to progress in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and humans.

verses.heading: John the Baptizer Prepares the Way for YHWH / John the Baptizer Prepares the Way for YHWH
verses.text: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene,
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John the son of Zachariah in the wilderness.
He went into all the region around the Jordan River, preaching the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Y’all prepare the way of the Lord [YHWH]. Y’all make ʜɪꜱ paths straight.
Every valley will be filled. Every mountain and hill will be made low. The crooked will become straight, and the rough ways smooth.
And all humanity will see God’s salvation.’”
Then John said to the multitudes who went out to be baptized by him, “Y’all brood of vipers, who warned y’all to flee from the wrath to come?

Therefore, y’all must produce fruits worthy of repentance. And y’all shouldn’t start saying to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham for our father.’ For I tell y’all that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones!
Indeed, the ax is already laid at the root of the trees, and every tree that doesn’t produce beautiful fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.”
So the crowds asked him, “Then what should we do?”
He answered them, “Anyone who has two coats should share with someone who has none, and anyone who has food must do likewise.”
Tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they asked him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
He said to them, “Y’all shouldn’t collect more than what y’all are required to.”
Then some soldiers asked him, “What about us? What should we do?” He replied, “Y’all must not take money from anyone by force or make false accusations. And y’all should be content with your* wages.”
While the people were waiting expectantly, and everyone was wondering in their hearts about whether John was the Christ,

John answered them all, “I baptize y’all with water, but one who is stronger than I will come, and I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandals. He will baptize y’all with the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing fork is in his hand to cleanse his threshing floor and to gather the wheat into his barn, but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
Then with many other exhortations he proclaimed the good news to the people.
But John rebuked Herod the tetrarch, because of Herodias, his brother’s wife, and for all the evil things that Herod had done,
Herod added this to them all: he locked up John in prison.

verses.heading: The Baptism and Genealogy of Jesus / The Baptism and Genealogy of Jesus
verses.text: Now when all the people were baptized, Jesus also was baptized, and while he was praying, the sky was opened,
and the Holy Spirit descended on him in bodily form like a dove. And a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son. In you I am well pleased.”
Now Jesus was about thirty years old when he began his ministry. He was the son (as it was thought) of Joseph, the son of Heli,
the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Joseph, the son of Judah,
the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmadam, the son of Er,
the son of Jose, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliakim,
the son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon,
the son of Amminadab, the son of Ram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Kenan,
the son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.

verses.heading: The Temptation of Jesus / The Temptation of Jesus
verses.text: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,
where for forty days, he was tempted by the devil. He ate nothing in those days, and when they had ended, he was very hungry.
Then the devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread.”
Jesus answered him, “It is written, ‘A human must not live by bread alone.’”
verses.html: Jesus answered him, “It is written, ‘A human must not live by bread alone.’”

verses.text: Then the devil led him up to a high place and showed him all the empires of the world in an instant.
The devil said to him, “I will give you all their power and glory; for it has been handed over to me, and I can give it to anyone I want.
So then, if you worship me, it will all be yours.”
Jesus answered him, “It is written, ‘You are to worship the Lord [YHWH] your God, and you are to serve ʜɪᴍ only.’”
verses.html: Jesus answered him, “It is written, ‘You are to worship the Lord [YHWH] your God, and you are to serve ʜɪᴍ only.’”

verses.text: Then the devil led him to Jerusalem and had him stand on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here.
For it is written, ‘He will command his angels concerning you, to carefully guard you,’
and, ‘They will lift you up with their hands, so that you won’t strike your foot against a stone.’”
Jesus answered him, “It is said, ‘You must not test the Lord [YHWH] your God.’”
verses.html: Jesus answered him, “It is said, ‘You must not test the Lord [YHWH] your God.’”

verses.text: When the devil had finished every temptation, he left him until an opportune time.

verses.heading: Jesus Praised Everywhere But Nazareth / Jesus Praised Everywhere But Nazareth
verses.text: Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and news about him spread throughout the whole countryside.
He began teaching in their synagogues, and everyone praised him.
Then he went to Nazareth where he had been brought up. As was his custom, he went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day. He stood up to read,
and the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He unrolled the scroll and found the place where it was written,

“The Spirit of the Lord [YHWH] is on me, because ʜᴇ has anointed me to preach good news to the poor. Hᴇ has sent me to proclaim freedom for the captives, recovery of sight to the blind, to set free the oppressed,
verses.html:
“The Spirit of the Lord [YHWH] is on me,
because ʜᴇ has anointed me to preach
good news to the poor.
Hᴇ has sent me to proclaim
freedom for the captives,
recovery of sight to the blind,
to set free the oppressed,

verses.text: and to proclaim the year of the Lord’s [YHWH] favor.”
verses.html: and to proclaim the year of the Lord’s [YHWH] favor.”

verses.text: He rolled up the scroll and gave it back to the attendant, and then sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fastened on him.
He began by saying to them, “Today, this Scripture has been fulfilled in y’all’s hearing.”
verses.html: He began by saying to them, “Today, this Scripture has been fulfilled in y’all’s hearing.”

verses.text: All were speaking well about him and marveling at the gracious words that came from his mouth. Yet they said, “Isn’t this Joseph’s son?”
Jesus said to them, “No doubt y’all will quote to me this proverb, ‘Physician, heal yourself!’ and say, ‘Do here in your hometown what we heard you did in Capernaum.’”
verses.html: Jesus said to them, “No doubt y’all will quote to me this proverb, ‘Physician, heal yourself!’ and say, ‘Do here in your hometown what we heard you did in Capernaum.’”

verses.text: He continued, “Truly I tell y’all, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.
verses.html: He continued, “Truly I tell y’all, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.

verses.text: But in truth, I tell y’all that there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three and half years and there was a great famine came over all the land.
verses.html: But in truth, I tell y’all that there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three and half years and there was a great famine came over all the land.

verses.text: Yet Elijah wasn’t sent to any of them, but only to a widow in Zarephath, in the land of Sidon.
verses.html: Yet Elijah wasn’t sent to any of them, but only to a widow in Zarephath, in the land of Sidon.

verses.text: And there were many people with leprosy in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet none of them were cleansed—only Naaman the Syrian.”
verses.html: And there were many people with leprosy in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet none of them were cleansed—only Naaman the Syrian.”

verses.text: When they heard this, all the people in the synagogue were filled with rage.
They got up and drove him out of the city, leading him to the edge of the hill on which their city was built, in order to throw him off the cliff.
But he passed right through them and went on his way.

verses.heading: Jesus Heals Throughout Capernaum / Jesus Heals Throughout Capernaum
verses.text: Then he went down to Capernaum, a town of Galilee. He was teaching them on the Sabbath day,
and they were struck with amazement at his teaching, because his words had authority.
In the synagogue there was a man possessed by an unclean demonic spirit who cried out with a loud voice,
“Go away! What do we have to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!”
Jesus rebuked him, “Be silent and come out of him!” Then the demon threw the man down in the middle of them and came out without injuring him.
verses.html: Jesus rebuked him, “Be silent and come out of him!” Then the demon threw the man down in the middle of them and came out without injuring him.

verses.text: Stunning wonder came over them all, and they said to one another, “What is this message? For he commands the unclean spirits with authority and power, and they come out!”
So news about him spread to every place in the surrounding region.
Jesus left the synagogue and went to Simon’s house. Now Simon’s mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and they begged him to help her.
He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. She got up immediately and began to serve them.
As the sun was setting, the people brought all those who were sick with various diseases to Jesus, and he laid his hands on every one of them and healed them.
Demons also came out of many people, crying out, “You are the Son of God!” But he rebuked them and didn’t allow them to speak, because they knew he was the Christ.
The next morning, Jesus left and went to a secluded place. The crowds were looking for him, and when they came to him, they tried to keep him from leaving them.
But he told them, “I must proclaim the good news of the Empire of God to the other towns also, because this is why I was sent.”
verses.html: But he told them, “I must proclaim the good news of the Empire of God to the other towns also, because this is why I was sent.”

verses.text: So he continued preaching in the synagogues of Judea.

verses.heading: Fishermen Follow Jesus / Fishermen Follow Jesus
verses.text: Now Jesus was standing by the lake of Gennesaret, and the people were crowding around him to hear the word of God.
He saw two fisherman’s boats at the edge of the lake, whose owners had gotten out of them to wash their nets.
He got into Simon’s boat and asked him to put out a little from the land. Then he sat down and taught the crowd from the boat.
When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep, and then y’all let down your* nets for a catch.”
verses.html: When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep, and then y’all let down your* nets for a catch.”

verses.text: Simon answered him, “Master, we worked hard all night and caught nothing. But since you said the word, I will let down the nets.”
When they did this, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.
So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. They came and filled both boats so much that they began to sink.
When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’s knees and said, “Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man.”
For he and all his companions were astonished at the catch of fish which they had taken,
and so were Simon’s partners, James and John, sons of Zebedee. Then Jesus said to Simon, “Don’t be afraid. From now on you will be catching humans.”
verses.html:
and so were Simon’s partners, James and John, sons of Zebedee.
Then Jesus said to Simon, “Don’t be afraid. From now on you will be catching humans.”

verses.text: When they had brought their boats to shore, they left everything and followed him.

verses.heading: A Man With Leprosy Asks If Jesus Is Willing / A Man With Leprosy Asks If Jesus Is Willing
verses.text: While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man was there covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face and begged him, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
Jesus stretched out his hand and touched the man, saying, “I am willing. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
verses.html:
Jesus stretched out his hand and touched the man, saying, “I am willing. Be made clean.”
Immediately the leprosy left him.

verses.text: Then Jesus ordered him, “Tell no one. Go and show yourself to the priest and make an offering for your cleansing just as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
verses.html: Then Jesus ordered him, “Tell no one. Go and show yourself to the priest and make an offering for your cleansing just as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

verses.text: But news about him spread even more, and large crowds came together to hear him and to be healed of their sicknesses.
But Jesus often withdrew to the wilderness and prayed.

verses.heading: Friends Bring a Paralyzed Man to Jesus / Friends Bring a Paralyzed Man to Jesus
verses.text: One day, while he was teaching, some Pharisees and teachers of the law who had come from every village of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem, were sitting nearby. And the power of the Lord was with Jesus to heal.
Just then, some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a cot, and they were trying to bring him in to lay before Jesus.
When they couldn’t find a way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up to the roof and lowered him on his cot through the tiles into the middle of the crowd in front of Jesus.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to him, “Man, your sins are forgiven you.”
verses.html: When Jesus saw their faith, he said to him, “Man, your sins are forgiven you.”

verses.text: The scribes and the Pharisees began to think to themselves, “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?”
But Jesus, aware of their thoughts, answered them, “Why are y’all thinking like this in y’all’s hearts?
verses.html: But Jesus, aware of their thoughts, answered them, “Why are y’all thinking like this in y’all’s hearts?

verses.text: Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk?’
verses.html: Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk?’

verses.text: But so that y’all may know that the Son of Humanity has authority on earth to forgive sins,” —he said to the paralyzed man, “I tell you, get up, take up your cot, and go home.”
verses.html: But so that y’all may know that the Son of Humanity has authority on earth to forgive sins,” —he said to the paralyzed man, “I tell you, get up, take up your cot, and go home.”

verses.text: Immediately he stood up in front of them, took up what he had been laying on, and went home glorifying God.
They were all struck with amazement and glorified God. They were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen remarkable things today.”

verses.heading: Jesus Calls Levi and Gets Questioned / Jesus Calls Levi and Gets Questioned
verses.text: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, and said to him, “Follow me!”
verses.html: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, and said to him, “Follow me!”

verses.text: So, leaving everything behind, he got up and followed him.
Levi held a massive banquet for Jesus in his house. There was a large crowd of tax collectors and others were reclining at the table with them.
But the Pharisees and their scribes complained to his disciples, “Why do y’all eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus answered them, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but those who are sick.
verses.html: Jesus answered them, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but those who are sick.

verses.text: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
verses.html: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

verses.heading: Jesus Questioned About Fasting / Jesus Questioned About Fasting
verses.text: They said to him, “John’s disciples often fast and pray, and the disciples of the Pharisees do the same, but yours eat and drink.”
He said to them, “Y’all can’t make the friends of the bridegroom fast while he is with them, can y’all?
verses.html: He said to them, “Y’all can’t make the friends of the bridegroom fast while he is with them, can y’all?

verses.text: But the time will come when the groom will be taken away from them, then in those days they will fast.”
verses.html: But the time will come when the groom will be taken away from them, then in those days they will fast.”

verses.text: He also told them a parable. “No one tears a piece from a new garment and puts it on an old garment. Otherwise, they will have torn the new, and the piece from the new will not match the old.
verses.html: He also told them a parable. “No one tears a piece from a new garment and puts it on an old garment. Otherwise, they will have torn the new, and the piece from the new will not match the old.

verses.text: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the new wine will burst the skins, it will spill out, and the skins will be destroyed.
verses.html: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the new wine will burst the skins, it will spill out, and the skins will be destroyed.

verses.text: Instead new wine must be put into fresh wine skins.
verses.html: Instead new wine must be put into fresh wine skins.

verses.text: And no one after drinking old wine wants the new, for they will say, ‘The old is better.’”
verses.html: And no one after drinking old wine wants the new, for they will say, ‘The old is better.’”

verses.heading: The Lord of the Sabbath / The Lord of the Sabbath
verses.text: One Sabbath, Jesus was going through the grain fields, and his disciples started picking the heads of grain, rubbing them in their hands, and eating them.
But some of the Pharisees said to them, “Why are y’all doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath day?”
Jesus answered them, “Haven’t y’all read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
verses.html: Jesus answered them, “Haven’t y’all read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?

verses.text: He entered the house of God, and took and ate the sacred bread which is not lawful for anyone but priests to eat. He also gave some to his companions.”
verses.html: He entered the house of God, and took and ate the sacred bread which is not lawful for anyone but priests to eat. He also gave some to his companions.”

verses.text: Then Jesus said to them, “The Son of Humanity is Lord of the Sabbath.”
verses.html: Then Jesus said to them, “The Son of Humanity is Lord of the Sabbath.”

verses.text: On another Sabbath, he went into the synagogue and was teaching, and there was a man whose right hand was shriveled.
The scribes and the Pharisees watched him to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find a reason to accuse him.
But he knew their thoughts, so he said to the man with the shriveled hand, “Get up and stand here in the middle.” So he got up and stood there.
verses.html: But he knew their thoughts, so he said to the man with the shriveled hand, “Get up and stand here in the middle.” So he got up and stood there.

verses.text: Then Jesus said to them, “I’m going to ask y’all something: on the Sabbath, is it lawful to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to destroy it?”
verses.html: Then Jesus said to them, “I’m going to ask y’all something: on the Sabbath, is it lawful to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to destroy it?”

verses.text: He looked around at them all, and then said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did, and his hand was restored.
verses.html: He looked around at them all, and then said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did, and his hand was restored.

verses.text: But they were filled with rage, and they started to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus.

verses.heading: Naming The Twelve Apostles / Naming The Twelve Apostles
verses.text: During those days, Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and he spent the whole night in prayer to God.
When morning came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles:
Simon (whom he also named Peter), Andrew, his brother James, John, Philip, Bartholomew,
Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon who was called the Zealot,
Judas the son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.

verses.heading: Blessings and Woes / Blessings and Woes
verses.text: He came down with them and stood on a level place with a large crowd of his disciples and a great number of people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon.
They came to hear him and be healed of their diseases, and those who were troubled by unclean spirits were made well.
All the crowd was trying to touch him, because power was coming out of him and healing them all.
Then looking up at his disciples, he said: “Blessed are the poor, for y’all’s is the Empire of God.
verses.html:
Then looking up at his disciples, he said:
“Blessed are the poor,
for y’all’s is the Empire of God.

verses.text: Blessed are those who hunger now, for y’all will be satisfied. Blessed are those who weep now, for y’all will laugh.
verses.html:
Blessed are those who hunger now,
for y’all will be satisfied.
Blessed are those who weep now,
for y’all will laugh.

verses.text: Blessed are y’all when humans hate you*, and when they exclude and mock y’all, and reject y’all’s name as evil because of the Son of Humanity.
verses.html:
Blessed are y’all when humans hate you*,
and when they exclude and mock y’all,
and reject y’all’s name as evil because of the Son of Humanity.

verses.text: Y’all should rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because y’all’s reward is great in heaven. For their ancestors treated the prophets the same way.
verses.html: Y’all should rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because y’all’s reward is great in heaven. For their ancestors treated the prophets the same way.

verses.text: “But woe to y’all who are rich! For y’all have received y’all’s comfort.
verses.html:
“But woe to y’all who are rich!
For y’all have received y’all’s comfort.

verses.text: Woe to y’all who are well-fed now, for y’all will be hungry. Woe to y’all who laugh now, for y’all will mourn and weep.
verses.html:
Woe to y’all who are well-fed now,
for y’all will be hungry.
Woe to y’all who laugh now,
for y’all will mourn and weep.

verses.text: Woe to y’all when humans speak well of y’all, for their ancestors treated the false prophets the same way.
verses.html:
Woe to y’all when humans speak well of y’all,
for their ancestors treated the false prophets the same way.

verses.heading: Love Y’all’s Enemies / Love Y’all’s Enemies
verses.text: “But I say to y’all who are listening: Y’all should love y’all’s enemies, do good to those who hate y’all,
verses.html: “But I say to y’all who are listening: Y’all should love y’all’s enemies, do good to those who hate y’all,

verses.text: bless those who curse y’all, and pray for those who mistreat y’all.
verses.html: bless those who curse y’all, and pray for those who mistreat y’all.

verses.text: Whoever strikes you on the cheek, offer them the other also. Whoever takes away your cloak, don’t withhold your shirt from them.
verses.html: Whoever strikes you on the cheek, offer them the other also. Whoever takes away your cloak, don’t withhold your shirt from them.

verses.text: Give to everyone who asks you, and whoever takes what is yours, don’t demand it back.
verses.html: Give to everyone who asks you, and whoever takes what is yours, don’t demand it back.

verses.text: “Y’all are to do for others what y’all want them to do for you*.
verses.html: “Y’all are to do for others what y’all want them to do for you*.

verses.text: “If y’all love those who love y’all, what credit is that to y’all? Even sinners love those who love them.
verses.html: “If y’all love those who love y’all, what credit is that to y’all? Even sinners love those who love them.

verses.text: And if y’all do good for those who do good for y’all, what credit is that to y’all? Even sinners do that.
verses.html: And if y’all do good for those who do good for y’all, what credit is that to y’all? Even sinners do that.

verses.text: And if y’all lend to those from whom y’all hope to be repaid, what credit is that to y’all? Even sinners lend to sinners in order to be repaid the same amount.
verses.html: And if y’all lend to those from whom y’all hope to be repaid, what credit is that to y’all? Even sinners lend to sinners in order to be repaid the same amount.

verses.text: But y’all should love y’all’s enemies, and y’all should do good and lend expecting nothing in return. Then y’all’s reward will be great, and y’all will be children of the Most High, because ʜᴇ is kind toward the unthankful and evil.
verses.html: But y’all should love y’all’s enemies, and y’all should do good and lend expecting nothing in return. Then y’all’s reward will be great, and y’all will be children of the Most High, because ʜᴇ is kind toward the unthankful and evil.

verses.text: “Therefore y’all are to be merciful, just as your* Father is also merciful.
verses.html:
“Therefore y’all are to be merciful,
just as your* Father is also merciful.

verses.heading: On Judging Others / On Judging Others
verses.text: Don’t y’all judge, and y’all won’t be judged. Don’t y’all condemn, and y’all won’t be condemned. Y’all forgive, and y’all will be forgiven.
verses.html: Don’t y’all judge, and y’all won’t be judged. Don’t y’all condemn, and y’all won’t be condemned. Y’all forgive, and y’all will be forgiven.

verses.text: “Y’all should give, and it will be given to y’all. An excellent measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be poured into your lap. For the measure y’all use will be the measure y’all get back.”
verses.html: “Y’all should give, and it will be given to y’all. An excellent measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be poured into your lap. For the measure y’all use will be the measure y’all get back.”

verses.text: He also told them a parable. “Can the blind guide the blind? Won’t they both fall into a pit?
verses.html: He also told them a parable. “Can the blind guide the blind? Won’t they both fall into a pit?

verses.text: A student is not above the teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like their teacher.
verses.html: A student is not above the teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like their teacher.

verses.text: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but don’t notice the log in your own eye?
verses.html: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but don’t notice the log in your own eye?

verses.text: How can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck from your eye,’ when you yourself don’t see the log in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the log from your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck in your brother’s eye.
verses.html: How can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck from your eye,’ when you yourself don’t see the log in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the log from your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck in your brother’s eye.

verses.heading: People and Their Fruit / People and Their Fruit
verses.text: “A beautiful tree doesn’t produce rotten fruit, and likewise, a rotten tree doesn’t produce beautiful fruit.
verses.html: “A beautiful tree doesn’t produce rotten fruit, and likewise, a rotten tree doesn’t produce beautiful fruit.

verses.text: Each tree is known by its own fruit. For people don’t pick figs from thornbushes, or grapes from brambles.
verses.html: Each tree is known by its own fruit. For people don’t pick figs from thornbushes, or grapes from brambles.

verses.text: The good human produces good from the good treasure in their heart, while the evil person produces evil from evil treasure in their heart. For out of the abundance of the heart, one’s mouth speaks.
verses.html: The good human produces good from the good treasure in their heart, while the evil person produces evil from evil treasure in their heart. For out of the abundance of the heart, one’s mouth speaks.

verses.heading: Choosing a Wise Foundation / Choosing a Wise Foundation
verses.text: “Why do y’all call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and yet y’all don’t do what I say?
verses.html: “Why do y’all call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and yet y’all don’t do what I say?

verses.text: Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words and does them, I will show y’all what they are like.
verses.html: Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words and does them, I will show y’all what they are like.

verses.text: They are like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood came, the torrent broke against that house and could not shake it, because it was finely built.
verses.html: They are like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood came, the torrent broke against that house and could not shake it, because it was finely built.

verses.text: But the one who hears but doesn’t do is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. When the torrent broke against that house, it immediately collapsed and was completely destroyed.”
verses.html: But the one who hears but doesn’t do is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. When the torrent broke against that house, it immediately collapsed and was completely destroyed.”

verses.heading: A Centurion Illustrates Faith / A Centurion Illustrates Faith
verses.text: After he had completed all his teaching to the people who were listening, he entered Capernaum.
A certain centurion had a servant whom he highly regarded, who was sick and about to die.
When he heard about Jesus, he sent some elders of the Jews to ask him to come and heal his servant.
When they came to Jesus, they pleaded with him earnestly, “He is worthy for you to grant this for him,
because he loves our ethnic group, and he built our synagogue for us.”
So Jesus went with them. When he was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to say to him, “Lord, don’t trouble yourself, for I am not worthy for you to come under my roof.
That is why I didn’t even consider myself worthy to come to you. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
For I also am a human under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell this one, ‘Go!’ and he goes, and to another, ‘Come!’ and he comes. I say to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
When Jesus heard this, he marveled at him. Then he turned to the crowd following him and said, “I tell y’all, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”
verses.html: When Jesus heard this, he marveled at him. Then he turned to the crowd following him and said, “I tell y’all, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”

verses.text: When those who had been sent returned to the house, they found that the servant was well.

verses.heading: Jesus Raises a Widow’s Only Son / Jesus Raises a Widow’s Only Son
verses.text: Soon afterward, he went to a city called Nain. Many of his disciples and a large crowd went with him.
As he approached the town gate, a dead person was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. A large crowd from the town was with her.
When the Lord saw her, he felt gut-wrenching sympathy for her and said to her, “Don’t cry.”
verses.html: When the Lord saw her, he felt gut-wrenching sympathy for her and said to her, “Don’t cry.”

verses.text: Then he came up and touched the open coffin, and the bearers stood still. He said, “Young man, I say to you, get up!”
verses.html: Then he came up and touched the open coffin, and the bearers stood still. He said, “Young man, I say to you, get up!”

verses.text: The dead man sat up and began to speak, and then Jesus gave him to his mother.
Fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us!” and, “God has come to help his people!”
This news about him spread throughout all of Judea and the surrounding region.

verses.heading: Jesus Affirms John the Baptizer’s Ministry / Jesus Affirms John the Baptizer’s Ministry
verses.text: John’s disciples told him about all these things. So John summoned two of them
and sent them to the Lord to ask, “Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for someone else?”
When the men came to Jesus, they said, “John the Baptizer has sent us to you, saying, ‘Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for someone else?’”
At that very time, he cured many people of diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and he gave sight to many who were blind.

Jesus answered them, “Y’all go and tell John what you* have seen and heard: that the blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and good news is preached to the poor.
verses.html: Jesus answered them, “Y’all go and tell John what you* have seen and heard: that the blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and good news is preached to the poor.

verses.text: Blessed is anyone who does not stumble on account of me.”
verses.html: Blessed is anyone who does not stumble on account of me.”

verses.text: When John’s messengers had left, Jesus began to tell the crowd about John, “What did y’all go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
verses.html: When John’s messengers had left, Jesus began to tell the crowd about John, “What did y’all go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?

verses.text: But what did y’all go out to see? A human dressed in plush clothing? Look, those who wear fancy clothes and live in luxury are in the palaces.
verses.html: But what did y’all go out to see? A human dressed in plush clothing? Look, those who wear fancy clothes and live in luxury are in the palaces.

verses.text: But what did y’all go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell y’all, and much more than a prophet.
verses.html: But what did y’all go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell y’all, and much more than a prophet.

verses.text: This is the one of whom it is written, ‘Look, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’
verses.html:
This is the one of whom it is written,
‘Look, I send my messenger before your face,
who will prepare your way before you.’

verses.text: “For I tell y’all, among those born of women there is not a greater prophet than John. Yet the one who is least in the Empire of God is greater than he.”
verses.html: “For I tell y’all, among those born of women there is not a greater prophet than John. Yet the one who is least in the Empire of God is greater than he.”

verses.text: When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they acknowledged God’s justice, because they had been baptized by John.
But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God for them, because they had not been baptized by John.
Jesus continued, “To what then should I compare the humans of this generation? What are they like?
verses.html: Jesus continued, “To what then should I compare the humans of this generation? What are they like?

verses.text: They are like children who sit in the marketplace and call to one another, saying, ‘We played the flute for y’all, and y’all didn’t dance. We sang a mourning song, and y’all didn’t weep.’
verses.html:
They are like children who sit in the marketplace and call to one another, saying,
‘We played the flute for y’all,
and y’all didn’t dance.
We sang a mourning song,
and y’all didn’t weep.’

verses.text: For John the Baptizer came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and y’all say, ‘He has a demon.’
verses.html: For John the Baptizer came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and y’all say, ‘He has a demon.’

verses.text: The Son of Humanity has come eating and drinking, and y’all say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
verses.html: The Son of Humanity has come eating and drinking, and y’all say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’

verses.text: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”
verses.html: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”

verses.heading: A Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus’s Feet / A Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus’s Feet
verses.text: One of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him. So he went to the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.
Then a woman of that town who was a sinner learned that Jesus was reclining in the Pharisee’s house. So she brought an alabaster jar of perfume
and stood behind him at his feet weeping. She began to wet his feet with her tears, and she wiped them with her hair, kissed his feet, and anointed them with the perfume.
Now when the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, he would have known who and what kind of woman is touching him, that she is a sinner.”
Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” “Say it, teacher,” he replied.
verses.html:
Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.”
“Say it, teacher,” he replied.

verses.text: “A certain lender had two debtors. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
verses.html: “A certain lender had two debtors. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.

verses.text: Neither had enough to repay, so he forgave the debts them both. Now which of them will love him more?”
verses.html: Neither had enough to repay, so he forgave the debts them both. Now which of them will love him more?”

verses.text: Simon answered, “I suppose the one he forgave more.” Jesus said to him, “You have judged correctly.”
verses.html:
Simon answered, “I suppose the one he forgave more.”
Jesus said to him, “You have judged correctly.”

verses.text: Turning to the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I came into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet. But she has wet my feet with her tears, and wiped them with her hair.
verses.html: Turning to the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I came into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet. But she has wet my feet with her tears, and wiped them with her hair.

verses.text: You did not give me a kiss, but since the time I came in, she has not stopped kissing my feet.
verses.html: You did not give me a kiss, but since the time I came in, she has not stopped kissing my feet.

verses.text: You didn’t anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with perfume.
verses.html: You didn’t anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with perfume.

verses.text: Therefore I tell you, she sinned much, but they have been forgiven, for she loved much. But whoever is forgiven little, loves little.”
verses.html: Therefore I tell you, she sinned much, but they have been forgiven, for she loved much. But whoever is forgiven little, loves little.”

verses.text: Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
verses.html: Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”

verses.text: Those who were at the table with him began to say among themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
verses.html: He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”

verses.heading: Several Women Support Christ’s Mission / Several Women Support Christ’s Mission
verses.text: After this, he traveled around through towns and villages, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the Empire of God. The twelve were with him
and also some women who had been healed of evil spirits and sicknesses: Mary (called Magdalene) from whom seven demons had gone out,
Joanna the wife of Chuzas (Herod’s house manager), Susanna, and many others who provided for them from their resources.

verses.heading: The Parable of the Sower / The Parable of the Sower
verses.text: When a large crowd came together and people from every town were traveling to him, he spoke to them in a parable:
“A farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed the seed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled on, and the wild birds devoured it.
verses.html: “A farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed the seed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled on, and the wild birds devoured it.

verses.text: Other seed fell on the rocky ground, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.
verses.html: Other seed fell on the rocky ground, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.

verses.text: Other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew with it and choked it.
verses.html: Other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew with it and choked it.

verses.text: Other seed fell on the good soil and grew and produced a crop one hundred times as much.” When he said this, he called out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!”
verses.html:
Other seed fell on the good soil and grew and produced a crop one hundred times as much.”
When he said this, he called out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!”

verses.text: Then his disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”
He said, “The mysteries of the Empire of God have been given to y’all to know, but to the others, it is given in parables, so that ‘seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.’
verses.html: He said, “The mysteries of the Empire of God have been given to y’all to know, but to the others, it is given in parables, so that ‘seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.’

verses.text: “Now the parable means this: The seed is the word of God.
verses.html: “Now the parable means this: The seed is the word of God.

verses.text: Those along the road are those who hear, and then the devil comes and takes away the word from their heart, so that they will not believe and be saved.
verses.html: Those along the road are those who hear, and then the devil comes and takes away the word from their heart, so that they will not believe and be saved.

verses.text: Those on the rocky soil are those who hear the word with joy when they hear it, but have no root. They believe for a while, but fall away in the time of temptation.
verses.html: Those on the rocky soil are those who hear the word with joy when they hear it, but have no root. They believe for a while, but fall away in the time of temptation.

verses.text: The seed that fell among the thorns are those who have heard, but as they go on their way, they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life, so they bring no fruit to maturity.
verses.html: The seed that fell among the thorns are those who have heard, but as they go on their way, they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life, so they bring no fruit to maturity.

verses.text: But the seed that fell on the excellent ground, these are the ones who have an honest and excellent heart, who hear the word, hold it tightly, and through perseverance, produce fruit.
verses.html: But the seed that fell on the excellent ground, these are the ones who have an honest and excellent heart, who hear the word, hold it tightly, and through perseverance, produce fruit.

verses.heading: A Lamp on a Stand / A Lamp on a Stand
verses.text: “No one lights a lamp and then covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it on a stand, so that those who come in can see the light.
verses.html: “No one lights a lamp and then covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it on a stand, so that those who come in can see the light.

verses.text: For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, nor anything secret that will not be known and come to be recognized.
verses.html: For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, nor anything secret that will not be known and come to be recognized.

verses.text: Therefore, y’all should listen carefully. For whoever has will be given more, and whoever doesn’t have, even what they think they have will be taken from them.”
verses.html: Therefore, y’all should listen carefully. For whoever has will be given more, and whoever doesn’t have, even what they think they have will be taken from them.”

verses.heading: Jesus’s Mother and Brothers / Jesus’s Mother and Brothers
verses.text: Now Jesus’s mother and brothers came to him, but they could not get near him because of the crowd.
Some people told him, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you.”
But he answered them, “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it.”
verses.html: But he answered them, “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it.”

verses.heading: Nature Obeys Its Creator / Nature Obeys Its Creator
verses.text: One day, Jesus got into a boat with his disciples and said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side of the lake.” So they launched out.
verses.html: One day, Jesus got into a boat with his disciples and said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side of the lake.” So they launched out.

verses.text: As they were sailing, he fell asleep. A fierce wind storm came down on the lake, and they began to take on water and were in great danger.
They went and woke Jesus, saying, “Master, Master, we are going to die!” He got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters, and then they ceased, and all was calm.
He said to them, “Where is y’all’s faith?” They were terrified and they marveled, saying to one another, “Who even is this? He commands the winds and the water, and they obey him?”
verses.html:
He said to them, “Where is y’all’s faith?”
They were terrified and they marveled, saying to one another, “Who even is this? He commands the winds and the water, and they obey him?”

verses.heading: The Demons Obey the Lord / The Demons Obey the Lord
verses.text: Then they sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, which is across from Galilee.
When Jesus stepped ashore, a man from the town who had demons came to meet him. He had not worn clothing for a long time, and did not live in a house, but in the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before him, shouting with a loud voice, “What do I have to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, don’t torment me!”

For Jesus had commanded the impure spirit to come out of the man. It has seized him many times, and he was chained hand and foot and kept under guard, but he would break the bonds, and the demon would drive him into deserted places.
Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He said, “Legion,” for many demons had entered him.
verses.html:
Jesus asked him, “What is your name?”
He said, “Legion,” for many demons had entered him.

verses.text: They begged him that he would not order them to go into the abyss.
Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding on the hillside. The demons begged Jesus to allow them to enter the swine, and he gave them permission.
When the demons came out of the man, they entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and were drowned.
When the herdsmen saw what had happened, they fled and reported this in the town and countryside.
So the people went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out, sitting at Jesus’s feet, dressed and in his right mind—and they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them how the demon-possessed man had been made well.
Then all the people of the surrounding region of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to depart from them, for they were very gripped by great fear. So he got into the boat and returned.
But the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him that he might go with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,
“Return to your home and tell the story of what great things God has done for you.” He set off, proclaiming throughout the whole town what great things Jesus had done for him.
verses.html: “Return to your home and tell the story of what great things God has done for you.” He set off, proclaiming throughout the whole town what great things Jesus had done for him.

verses.heading: Jesus Offers Healing and Resurrection to Two Women / Jesus Offers Healing and Resurrection to Two Women
verses.text: When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.
A man named Jairus, a synagogue official, came and fell down at Jesus’s feet, begging him to come into his house,
because his one and only daughter, who was about twelve years old, was dying. But as Jesus was on his way, the crowd pressed against him.
A woman was there who had been hemorrhaging blood for twelve years, but could not be healed by anyone.
She came behind him and touched the edge of his cloak. Immediately her bleeding stopped.
Jesus said, “Who touched me?” When they all denied it, Peter and those with him said, “Master, the people are crowding and pressing in on you.”
verses.html:
Jesus said, “Who touched me?”
When they all denied it, Peter and those with him said, “Master, the people are crowding and pressing in on you.”

verses.text: But Jesus said, “Someone did touch me, for I knew that power has gone out from me.”
verses.html: But Jesus said, “Someone did touch me, for I knew that power has gone out from me.”

verses.text: When the woman saw that she could not go unnoticed, she came trembling and fell down before him. In the presence of all the people, she openly shared why she had touched him, and how she had been healed instantly.
He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
verses.html: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”

verses.text: While he was still speaking, someone from the synagogue official’s house came and said to him, “Your daughter is dead. Don’t trouble the Teacher anymore.”
But when Jesus heard this, he said to him, “Don’t be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed.”
verses.html: But when Jesus heard this, he said to him, “Don’t be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed.”

verses.text: When he arrived at the house, Jesus didn’t allow anyone to go in with him, except Peter, John, James, and the child’s father and mother.
Everyone was crying and mourning for her, but he said, “Y’all stop crying. She is not dead, but is asleep.”
verses.html: Everyone was crying and mourning for her, but he said, “Y’all stop crying. She is not dead, but is asleep.”

verses.text: They began laughing at him, because they knew she was dead.
But he took her by the hand, and said, “Child, arise!”
verses.html: But he took her by the hand, and said, “Child, arise!”

verses.text: Her spirit returned, and she immediately got up. Then Jesus told them to give her something to eat.
Her parents were astonished, but he ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.

verses.heading: Jesus Sends Out the Twelve in Power / Jesus Sends Out the Twelve in Power
verses.text: Jesus called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons and to cure diseases,
and he sent them out to preach the Empire of God and to heal the sick.
He said to them, “Y’all are to take nothing for your journey—no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, not even an extra shirt.
verses.html: He said to them, “Y’all are to take nothing for your journey—no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, not even an extra shirt.

verses.text: Whatever house y’all enter, stay there, until y’all leave that town.
verses.html: Whatever house y’all enter, stay there, until y’all leave that town.

verses.text: Wherever they don’t receive y’all, when y’all leave that town, shake off the dust from y’all’s feet as a testimony against them.”
verses.html: Wherever they don’t receive y’all, when y’all leave that town, shake off the dust from y’all’s feet as a testimony against them.”

verses.text: So they departed and went from village to village, preaching the gospel and healing people everywhere.
Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was happening, and he was nonplussed, because some said that John had been raised from the dead,
and some that Elijah had appeared, and others that one of the ancient prophets had risen again.
Herod said, “I beheaded John, so then who is this I hear such things about?” And he tried to see him.

verses.heading: Jesus Feeds the Five Thousand / Jesus Feeds the Five Thousand
verses.text: When the apostles returned, they gave an account of everything they had done. Taking them with him, he withdrew privately to a town called Bethsaida.
But the crowds learned about this, and they followed him. He welcomed them, spoke to them about the Empire of God, and cured those who needed healing.

As the day was ending, the Twelve came and said to him, “You must send the crowd away, so that they can go into the surrounding villages and countryside and find lodging and food, because we are in a remote place.”
But he told them, “Y’all give them something to eat!” They said, “We only have five loaves and two fish, unless we go and buy food for all these people.”
verses.html:
But he told them, “Y’all give them something to eat!”
They said, “We only have five loaves and two fish, unless we go and buy food for all these people.”

verses.text: (About five thousand men were there.) He said to his disciples, “Y’all have them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
verses.html:
(About five thousand men were there.)
He said to his disciples, “Y’all have them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”

verses.text: They did so, and had them all sit down.
He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to the sky, he blessed them and broke them. Then he gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
They all ate and were satisfied. Then they gathered up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.

verses.heading: Jesus, the Christ Who Will Die and Be Raised / Jesus, the Christ Who Will Die and Be Raised
verses.text: Once when Jesus was praying in private and the disciples were near him, he asked them, “Who do the crowds say that I am?”
verses.html: Once when Jesus was praying in private and the disciples were near him, he asked them, “Who do the crowds say that I am?”

verses.text: They answered, “Some say ‘John the Baptizer,’ but others, ‘Elijah,’ and still others, that one of the ancient prophets has risen again.”
He said to them, “But who do y’all say I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”
verses.html:
He said to them, “But who do y’all say I am?”
Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”

verses.text: But he warned them and instructed them not to tell this to anyone,
saying, “The Son of Humanity must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and he will be killed, and on the third day be raised up.”
verses.html: saying, “The Son of Humanity must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and he will be killed, and on the third day be raised up.”

verses.text: He said to them all, “Anyone who desires to follow come after must deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.
verses.html: He said to them all, “Anyone who desires to follow come after must deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.

verses.text: For whoever desires to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for my sake will save it.
verses.html: For whoever desires to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for my sake will save it.

verses.text: For what does it profit a human if they gain the whole world, but lose or forfeit their very self?
verses.html: For what does it profit a human if they gain the whole world, but lose or forfeit their very self?

verses.text: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words, the Son of Humanity will be ashamed of them when he comes in his glory, and in the glory of the Father and the holy angels.
verses.html: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words, the Son of Humanity will be ashamed of them when he comes in his glory, and in the glory of the Father and the holy angels.

verses.text: But I tell y’all the truth: Some who are standing here who not taste of death before they see the Empire of God.”
verses.html: But I tell y’all the truth: Some who are standing here who not taste of death before they see the Empire of God.”

verses.heading: The Transfiguration / The Transfiguration
verses.text: About eight days after they discussed this, Jesus took Peter, John, and James with him and went up onto the mountain to pray.
As he was praying, the appearance of his face changed, and his clothing became white like lightening.
Two men, Moses and Elijah, began talking with him.
They appeared in glory and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.
Now Peter his companions were overcome with sleep, but when they were fully awake, they saw his glory, and the two men standing with him.

As they were starting to leave Jesus, Peter said to him, “Master, it is excellent for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah”—not knowing what he was saying.
While he was saying this, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
A voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him, y’all!”
After the voice had spoken, they found that Jesus was alone. The disciples kept silent and told no one at that time anything of what they had seen.

verses.heading: Jesus Rebukes a Demon from a Man’s Only Son / Jesus Rebukes a Demon from a Man’s Only Son
verses.text: The next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.
A man from the crowd called out, “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only child.
A spirit seizes him, and he suddenly screams; it throws him into convulsions with foaming at the mouth. It hardly ever leaves him and is torturing him.
I begged your disciples to cast it out, and they could not do it.”
Jesus answered, “Unbelieving and perverse generation, how long must I stay with y’all and put up with y’all? Bring your son here.”
verses.html: Jesus answered, “Unbelieving and perverse generation, how long must I stay with y’all and put up with y’all? Bring your son here.”

verses.text: While the boy was approaching, the demon slammed him on the ground and threw him into a convulsion. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
They were all astonished at the majesty of God.

verses.heading: Jesus Predicts His Death Again / Jesus Predicts His Death Again
verses.text: “Let these words sink into y’all’s ears, for the Son of Humanity will be delivered into the hands of men.”
verses.html: “Let these words sink into y’all’s ears, for the Son of Humanity will be delivered into the hands of men.”

verses.text: But they didn’t understand this statement. Its meaning was hidden from them, so that they did not understand it, but they were afraid to ask him about it.
An argument arose among them about which of them might be the greatest.
Jesus, knowing what they were thinking in their hearts, took a little child whom he had stand beside him.
Then he said to them, “Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me. Whoever receives me receives the one who sent me. For whoever is least among all y’all, this is the great one.”
verses.html: Then he said to them, “Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me. Whoever receives me receives the one who sent me. For whoever is least among all y’all, this is the great one.”

verses.text: John answered, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he doesn’t follow us.”
Jesus said to him, “Y’all must not hinder him, for whoever is not against y’all is for y’all.”
verses.html: Jesus said to him, “Y’all must not hinder him, for whoever is not against y’all is for y’all.”

verses.heading: Jesus Rejected in Samaritan / Jesus Rejected in Samaritan
verses.text: As the day approached when he would be taken up into heaven, he firmly set his face to go to Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead of him, and they went and entered a Samaritan village to make preparations for him.
But the people didn’t receive him, because he was determined to go to Jerusalem.
When his disciples James and John saw this, they said, “Lord, do you want us to call fire to come down from heaven to destroy them?”
But Jesus turned and rebuked them,
and then they went to another village.

verses.heading: The Cost of Following Jesus / The Cost of Following Jesus
verses.text: As they walked the road, someone said to him, “I will follow you wherever you go, Lord.”
Jesus said to him, “The foxes have dens, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Humanity has no place to lay his head.”
verses.html: Jesus said to him, “The foxes have dens, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Humanity has no place to lay his head.”

verses.text: He said to another, “Follow me!” But he said, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
verses.html:
He said to another, “Follow me!”
But he said, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”

verses.text: But Jesus said to him, “Leave the dead to bury their own dead, but you go and proclaim the Empire of God.”
verses.html: But Jesus said to him, “Leave the dead to bury their own dead, but you go and proclaim the Empire of God.”

verses.text: Another also said, “I will follow you, Lord, but first, let me say goodbye to those at my house.”
But Jesus said to him, “No one who puts their hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the Empire of God.”
verses.html: But Jesus said to him, “No one who puts their hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the Empire of God.”

verses.heading: Jesus Sends Out the Seventy-Two / Jesus Sends Out the Seventy-Two
verses.text: After this, the Lord appointed seventy-two others, and sent them two by two ahead of him into every town and place where he was about to go.
Then he said to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few. Therefore y’all ask to the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into ʜɪꜱ harvest.
verses.html: Then he said to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few. Therefore y’all ask to the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into ʜɪꜱ harvest.

verses.text: Y’all go! I am sending y’all out as lambs among wolves.
verses.html: Y’all go! I am sending y’all out as lambs among wolves.

verses.text: Y’all shouldn’t bring a money belt or bag or sandals. And y’all shouldn’t greet anyone on the way.
verses.html: Y’all shouldn’t bring a money belt or bag or sandals. And y’all shouldn’t greet anyone on the way.

verses.text: Whenever y’all enter a house, first say, ‘Peace be to this house.’
verses.html: Whenever y’all enter a house, first say, ‘Peace be to this house.’

verses.text: If a person of peace is there, y’all’s peace will rest on them; but if not, it will return to y’all.
verses.html: If a person of peace is there, y’all’s peace will rest on them; but if not, it will return to y’all.

verses.text: Y’all are to stay at that same house, eating and drinking whatever they give, for the worker deserves their wages. Y’all must not go from house to house.
verses.html: Y’all are to stay at that same house, eating and drinking whatever they give, for the worker deserves their wages. Y’all must not go from house to house.

verses.text: When y’all enter a town and people welcome y’all, eat what is set before y’all.
verses.html: When y’all enter a town and people welcome y’all, eat what is set before y’all.

verses.text: Y’all heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘Empire of God has come near to y’all.’
verses.html: Y’all heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘Empire of God has come near to y’all.’

verses.text: But when y’all enter a town and they don’t welcome y’all, go out into its streets and say,
verses.html: But when y’all enter a town and they don’t welcome y’all, go out into its streets and say,

verses.text: ‘Even the dust from y’all’s town that clings to our feet, we wipe off against y’all. Yet y’all should know this, that the Empire of God has come near.’
verses.html: ‘Even the dust from y’all’s town that clings to our feet, we wipe off against y’all. Yet y’all should know this, that the Empire of God has come near.’

verses.text: I tell y’all, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.
verses.html: I tell y’all, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.

verses.text: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were done in y’all had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
verses.html: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were done in y’all had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

verses.text: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for y’all.
verses.html: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for y’all.

verses.text: And you, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Hades!
verses.html: And you, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Hades!

verses.text: Whoever listens to y’all listens to me, and whoever rejects y’all rejects me. Whoever rejects me rejects ʜɪᴍ who sent me.”
verses.html: Whoever listens to y’all listens to me, and whoever rejects y’all rejects me. Whoever rejects me rejects ʜɪᴍ who sent me.”

verses.text: The seventy-two returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name!”
He said to them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
verses.html: He said to them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.

verses.text: Look, I have given y’all authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the enemy’s power. Nothing will hurt y’all.
verses.html: Look, I have given y’all authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the enemy’s power. Nothing will hurt y’all.

verses.text: However, y’all shouldn’t rejoice that the spirits are subject to y’all, instead rejoice that y’all’s names are written in heaven.”
verses.html: However, y’all shouldn’t rejoice that the spirits are subject to y’all, instead rejoice that y’all’s names are written in heaven.”

verses.text: In that same hour, Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I publicly acknowledge you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in your sight.”
verses.html: In that same hour, Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I publicly acknowledge you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in your sight.”

verses.text: “All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, or who the Father is except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal ʜɪᴍ.”
verses.html: “All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, or who the Father is except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal ʜɪᴍ.”

verses.text: Turning to the disciples, he said privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see the things y’all see,
verses.html: Turning to the disciples, he said privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see the things y’all see,

verses.text: for I tell y’all that many prophets and kings desired to see what y’all see, but didn’t see them, and to hear what y’all hear, and didn’t hear them.”
verses.html: for I tell y’all that many prophets and kings desired to see what y’all see, but didn’t see them, and to hear what y’all hear, and didn’t hear them.”

verses.heading: The Good Samaritan / The Good Samaritan
verses.text: Now, a legal expert stood up to test Jesus, saying, “Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
verses.html: He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”

verses.text: He answered, “‘Love the Lord [YHWH] your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind,’ and ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
“You have answered correctly,” he told him. “Do this, and you will live.”
verses.html: “You have answered correctly,” he told him. “Do this, and you will live.”

verses.text: But wanting to justify himself, he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
Jesus replied, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell into the hands of robbers, who stripped him, beat him, and then departed, leaving him half dead.
verses.html: Jesus replied, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell into the hands of robbers, who stripped him, beat him, and then departed, leaving him half dead.

verses.text: By chance, a priest was going down that way, and when he saw the man, he passed by on the other side.
verses.html: By chance, a priest was going down that way, and when he saw the man, he passed by on the other side.

verses.text: Likewise, when a Levite came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.
verses.html: Likewise, when a Levite came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.
